newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv's Bark sees synergies from Morton merger.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv's Bark sees synergies from Morton merger.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment maker Autoliv AB said on Tuesday its planned merger with the vehicle safety unit of Morton International Inc would create synergy effects.
"The merger will lead to an overall reduction in investment costs and therefore an increased cash flow," former Autoliv managing director Gunnar Bark told the company's annual shareholders meeting.
"We can also help each other on new markets where neither of us have operations, or where one or the other is in the process of setting up a company," Bark said.
He named the United States, Germany and The Netherlands as examples of countries where production can be combined and costs reduced.
Other synergies from the merger include volume purchasing which could reduce buying costs, he said.
Bark has been proposed as the board head in the new company, which will be called Autoliv Inc.
Autoliv's shares have risen since news yesterday that U.S. tax authorities have given a preliminary nod of approval to the merger. The two companies expect the deal to be completed in early May.
